list.title: Docker hosts
list.desc: Remote Docker hosts that plugins such as Docker can manage, besides this machine.
list.emptyText: Add a remote Docker host to manage it from here. This machine is always available.

tcp-tls.name: Docker over TLS
tcp-tls.desc: The Docker daemon listens on a TCP port with TLS and client certificates (dockerd --tlsverify).
tcp-tls.addressHint: Host and port of the Docker API, usually 2376.
tcp-tls.insecureWarn: Anyone on the network path can read this connection and send commands to Docker, which means root on that machine. Use it only on a closed, trusted network.
tcp-tls.noCreds: Plain tcp has no certificates to set.

ssh.name: SSH
ssh.desc: Reach the Docker socket of a Linux host over SSH with a key. Docker does not need to listen on the network and nothing is installed on the host.
ssh.addressHint: Host and port of the SSH server.
ssh.userHint: The account must be allowed to use Docker (the docker group) and sshd must allow socket forwarding.

portainer-agent.name: Portainer agent
portainer-agent.desc: A host that already runs the Portainer agent. The Docker API is reached through the agent on its TLS port.
portainer-agent.addressHint: Host and port of the agent, usually 9001.

ervisio.name: Another Ervisio server
ervisio.desc: Another server running Ervisio. Calls run there, with its own plugins and rules, as a user you choose when you pair.
ervisio.addressHint: The address of the other server's web console.
ervisio.plainWarn: The pairing credential and every call travel unencrypted. Use it only to a server on this machine or on a closed network.

field.name: Name
field.kind: What kind of host is it?
field.caHint: PEM text of the CA that signed the server certificate. Leave empty to use this machine's trusted authorities.
field.clientCertHint: PEM text (cert.pem). Leave both certificate and key empty if the daemon does not ask for one.
field.clientKeyHint: PEM text (key.pem). It is stored on this server, readable only by root, and never shown again.
field.keepSecret: Already stored. Leave empty to keep it.
field.sshKeyHint: PEM or OpenSSH private key (id_ed25519). Stored on this server, readable only by root, and never shown again.
field.passphraseHint: Only if the key is protected. It is stored encrypted, because jobs and background work need it without you.
field.agentSecretHint: The AGENT_SECRET set on the agent. Without one, the agent ties itself to the first server that talks to it and refuses others, so setting one is strongly advised.
field.tokenHint: Create it on the other server in Settings > Environments > Pair another server. It works once and for 15 minutes.
field.pairedHint: Paired with {name}. To change the pairing, remove this environment and add it again.

trust.pinHint: Check the connection below and confirm the certificate fingerprint. Ervisio then refuses any other certificate.
trust.skipWarn: Without a check, anyone between this server and the host can pretend to be it. Prefer a CA or a pinned certificate.

probe.ssh: Check connection and show host key
probe.sshFound: The server presented this host key (SHA-256):

verify.tcp-tls: Compare it with the one on the Docker host (openssl x509 -in server-cert.pem -noout -fingerprint -sha256).
verify.ssh: Compare it with the host's own key (ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub, or the ECDSA or RSA file).
verify.portainer-agent: Agents use a self-signed certificate. Compare it with the one the agent logs or shows, if you can.
verify.ervisio: Compare it with the fingerprint shown on the other server when you created the pairing token.

probe.confirm: I checked it, this is the right server
probe.pinned: A fingerprint is already pinned. Check the connection again only if the host changed.
probe.plainServer: This server speaks plain http, so there is nothing to pin.
probe.localHttp: Plain http to this machine is fine. Elsewhere it needs the checkbox above.

access.all: Everyone who can use the plugin
access.hint: The plugin's own visibility still applies on top of this.
access.usersHint: Add a user name and press Enter
access.groupsHint: Add a group name and press Enter

pem.tooBig: {name} is too large for a certificate or key.

save.savedButOffline: {name} saved, but it is not reachable

remove.title: Remove {name}?
remove.text: Plugins can no longer use it. The stored credentials are deleted from this server. The remote host is not changed.
remove.textPaired: Plugins can no longer use it. The pairing is revoked on the other server and the stored credential is deleted here.

pair.title: Pair another server
pair.desc: Let another Ervisio server use this server's plugins, such as Docker, through a pairing.
pair.none: No server is paired with this one.
pair.dialogText: Create a one-time token, then paste it on the other server in Settings > Environments > Add environment > Another Ervisio server.
pair.userHint: Every call from the other server runs on this machine as this Linux user, with that user's rights and under this server's rules. It never gets administrator rights.
pair.securityNote: Whoever holds the pairing can do on this machine what {user} can do through the plugins installed here, such as managing Docker. Pair only servers you control. You can revoke it at any time.
pair.tokenText: Paste this token on the other server. It works once and expires in {minutes} minutes.
pair.copyFailed: Could not copy. Select the token and copy it by hand.
pair.expired: This token has expired. Close this window and create a new one.
pair.fingerprint: Certificate fingerprint of {server} (the other server asks you to confirm it):
pair.fingerprintHint: The other server shows the fingerprint it found. They must match.
pair.noTlsHint: This server serves plain http, so there is no certificate to compare. Pair only over a network you trust.
pair.runsAsNote: Calls will run as {user} on this machine.
pair.revokeText: {name} can no longer use this server. Its connections close at once. It can pair again with a new token.

network.title: Allow {plugin} to connect to a new address?
network.text: {plugin} asks to reach an address that is not part of its permissions.
network.exact: Only this exact host and port. Other addresses stay blocked.
network.plainOk: I understand that traffic to this address is not encrypted
network.needAdmin: Only an administrator can approve this. Ask one to open the plugin and allow it.

hosts.title: Approved network addresses
hosts.desc: Addresses plugins asked for beyond their own permissions, and an administrator approved. Revoking one takes effect the next time the plugin loads.
hosts.none: No extra address has been approved.
hosts.revokeText: {plugin} can no longer connect to it. It can ask again.
